Pier's open all night. Snapper bite at dusk, trout in the morning. Shrimp for both.
Mullet Bay Slam is every seventh day at the marina. Sign up before noon, weigh in before seven. Trent Marlowe wins because nobody shows up with anything.
There's a bonefish around Bird Key they call the Gray Ghost. Bright sun, the shallow flats, shrimp. You'll need a boat to get out there.
Marlowe's lobby guard clocks out at ten. After that it's one patrol and two cameras. The planters are your friends. That arowana likes lures.
Bayfront Park's fountain has the mayor's albino catfish. Night only. Hot dogs. Nobody has ever told the mayor.
The marina sells a used skiff. That's your ticket past the markers. Offshore it's squid or nothing.
Under the marina docks lives the Dock Monster. Night only. A watchman and his dog walk the docks after nine.
Old Glory feeds in daylight, way out past the markers. Bring the big-game rod or she'll make a fool of you.
The River Room keeps its dock lights on all night. Something big hangs out under them. The bartenders feed it.
